claims.text: Integrating cluster expansion with MD-based phonon-density-of-states analysis improves prediction accuracy for low lattice thermal conductivity relative to standalone MD or DFT.
The target material is a randomized, single-phase, equimolar high-entropy alloy with a BCC or FCC lattice and inherent chemical disorder.
Cluster expansion can quantify chemical short-range order.
MD-based PDOS calculations can use cluster-expansion results to estimate phonon scattering rates.
The proposed simulations are intended for temperatures relevant to thermal-insulation operation.
The framework assumes a single-phase solid solution without extensive phase separation or multiphase precipitates.
Configurational entropy from multiple principal elements produces local chemical ordering and lattice distortions.
Local chemical ordering and lattice distortions enhance phonon scattering.
Capturing chemical short-range-order effects on vibrational properties enables better quantification of phonon-scattering mechanisms.
Increased lattice distortion reduces phonon mean free paths.
Reduced phonon mean free paths and increased phonon scattering lower intrinsic thermal conductivity.
The integrated method will predict lower lattice thermal conductivity than conventional standalone MD or DFT.
The integrated method may improve prediction accuracy by approximately 10–20%.
The integrated predictions will correlate more closely with experimental thermal-insulation performance.
Standard standalone MD or DFT baselines do not explicitly account for chemical short-range-order effects.
The approach is primarily applicable to single-phase, chemically disordered HEA solid solutions.
The approach may not extend to precipitate-rich or multiphase HEAs because other scattering mechanisms may dominate.
The quantitative improvement and universality across HEA systems remain empirically unconfirmed.
The benchmark compares integrated-method and conventional-method predictions against measured thermal conductivity across multiple HEAs with characterized short-range order.

The hypothesis is falsified if the integrated method provides less than approximately 10% better agreement with experiment and no statistically significant improvement across multiple independent HEA systems.
